title: Florian Zeller Reveals the Making of Bunker With Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem
excerpt: Florian Zeller wrote Bunker with Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem in mind. The director discusses their demanding argument scene and the contributions of Stephen Graham and Eileen Atkins.
seo_title: Inside Bunker With Florian Zeller, Cruz and Bardem
seo_description: Florian Zeller explains the casting of Cruz and Bardem, a demanding 12-minute confrontation and the release plans for his new film Bunker.
body_md:
Florian Zeller has shared new details about the making of Bunker, his film starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem. In an interview published by Deadline on November 25, 2026, the writer-director discussed the origins of the project, the performances of its leading actors and the contributions of Stephen Graham and Dame Eileen Atkins.

## Writing for two performers

Cruz plays Sofía, a literary editor at a London publishing house, while Bardem portrays Miguel, an established architect and her husband. Their characters have been married for sixteen years. Zeller recalled meeting Cruz about an earlier project and later connecting with Bardem, who had expressed admiration for his work on The Father.

The filmmaker saw an opportunity to explore the relationship between fiction and the audience's awareness that the two actors are married in real life. He emphasized, however, that Bunker is not their personal story. Their shared history was a way to enrich the performances rather than a claim that the screenplay reflected their private lives.

Zeller singled out Cruz's ability to communicate complicated emotions without dialogue. He described the opening dinner sequence as an example of how Sofía's silent reactions reveal tensions that are not apparent in the conversation.

## A demanding confrontation

A pivotal argument between the central characters lasts approximately twelve minutes and took three days to film. Zeller recalled that Cruz had been apprehensive about the sequence and that Bardem helped her reach the emotional intensity required during filming.

Stephen Graham appears as Toby, the couple's neighbor. Zeller had admired Graham's performance in Adolescence and wanted an actor capable of introducing a credible sense of threat opposite Bardem while retaining recognizable humanity.

Eileen Atkins also appears in a brief scene with Cruz. Although Atkins had retired, Zeller arranged to shoot her appearance in London. It became the final scene filmed for the production.

## Fear and isolation

Zeller traced the film's inspiration to an article about a technology billionaire building a private bunker. He was interested in the contradiction between a business built around connecting people and an impulse to withdraw from the outside world. That idea informs the film's exploration of fear, security and isolation.

Sony Pictures Classics is scheduled to release Bunker in selected US cities on December 11, 2026, followed by a nationwide release on January 15, 2027. StudioCanal is scheduled to bring the film to the United Kingdom and Ireland on February 19, 2027.
